dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Methodically read every source file (main.rs, types.rs, decode.rs, runtime.rs, spec.rs) in full before editing, repeatedly paging through runtime.rs and spec.rs — genuine skeleton orientation, not skimming.

After first build produced an explicit map of what is stubbed vs buggy: exec_numeric unimplemented, Call/CallIndirect unimplemented, no SIMD, v128 lane accessors are stubs, lane_matches NaN handling — matches the codebase-map half of the level-8 anchor.

Understood the fixed public contract (spec.rs/main.rs untouched, kept backups), and located exactly where to wire the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode decoding and how v128 must slot into the existing Value/Instr model.

Non-obvious semantics (integer-overflow vs invalid-conversion, signed load sign-extension, v128.const in const-exprs) were discovered REACTIVELY via test failures and fixed, rather than pinned down from the spec beforehand.

No wabt-based encoding verification and no targeted spec-case probing to disambiguate lane order/rounding; SIMD correctness was reached by running family jsons and patching failures — falls short of the sustained proactive re-research described in the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's orientation to the provided skeleton is strong and explicit — it read all sources fully, enumerated exactly which functions were stubbed vs buggy, identified the frozen public contract, and located where v128/0xFD decoding must integrate (level-8 quality for the codebase-map half). However, the SIMD encoding and lane-semantics side (saturation, NaN, sign, conversions, const-exprs) was largely handled by prior knowledge and reactive test-driven fixes rather than deliberate spec research or wabt/encoding verification, which keeps it below a clean 8 and well short of the level-10 sustained re-research. This blend places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: Produced a numbered component-level plan (SimdOp enum, decode 0xFD, exec_numeric, Call, exec_simd, v128 helpers, lane_matches, assert_invalid) with MVP-then-SIMD framing, but SIMD collapsed into a single 'implement exec_simd' item — no ~15-family hierarchy or per-family done-checks.

SIMD implemented as two monolithic chunks (exec_simd for memory/const/splat/lane; exec_simd_2 for all arithmetic/comparisons) written to temp files and appended — coarse grouping, not family-by-family with spec-test checkpoints.
Clear sequencing of MVP correctness first: iterated over i32/block/call/conversions/memory and fixed br, sign extension, trap messages, memory cap before moving to SIMD — genuine phase ordering.

Ran all SIMD tests at once, then reactively drilled into individual family json files (store_lane, const, splat, lane) to localize/fix — per-family spec files used only as post-hoc debugging checkpoints, not planned milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced MVP before SIMD and had a numbered component plan with some dependency ordering (types→decode→runtime, v128.const in const-expr), placing it above the vague two-phase anchor (3). But SIMD was implemented as two monolithic code chunks and tested in aggregate rather than family-by-family with each family's spec_json as an exit check; per-family spec files appeared only reactively during debugging. That falls short of anchor 5's 'implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint,' landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: Established a failing baseline via i32.json before implementing, then ran individual per-family jsons (i32, block, call, f32, f64, conversions) right after implementing exec_numeric — the core incremental-verification loop.

Repeatedly used grep FAIL and 'grep -v inv' to isolate genuine bugs from validation failures per family, and ran the full /app/spec_json/*.json sweep multiple times to guard MVP families against regressions while progressing.

Drilled into individual FAIL @ line reasons to diagnose semantic edge cases: br label decrement, integer-overflow vs invalid-conversion, signed load extension, v128.const in const expressions — fix then re-run to green.
After MVP green, ran SIMD per-family jsons, localized store_lane failures to a const-expr issue, fixed, and re-ran the SIMD set to confirm.

Treated the aggregate score as a monitored signal (tracked 32825/34212 = 0.9595) and iterated toward exactly 1.0 rather than a one-shot final check — though partly by skipping/gaming assert_invalid rather than truly verifying that class.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran a sustained implement→run family json→read specific FAIL @ line→fix→re-run loop, periodically running the full runner to guard MVP against regression while adding SIMD, and diagnosed genuine semantic edge cases (sign extension, overflow vs invalid conversion, br decrement, NaN, const-expr) — matching the 8 anchor and reaching into the 10 anchor with edge-case diagnosis and aggregate-score monitoring. It falls short of a full 10 because it sidestepped the assert_invalid failure class (skipping rather than verifying) and partly gamed the count toward 1.0 rather than distinguishing and resolving every failure type, placing it at a strong 9.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: After the big implementation landed (jump from 2 to 376 passing), the agent immediately looped over multiple/all spec_json files to get per-file pass/fail counts and began categorizing failures (validation vs. real), establishing a concrete picture of what remained rather than assuming done.

Repeatedly re-ran the full per-file suite after each fix, tracking which families still had non-validation failures (memory 10, conversions 49, etc.) and reconciling counts as families went green — continuous per-family pass-count monitoring.

On moving to SIMD, enumerated exactly which SIMD families still failed and their counts (simd_const 5, simd_lane 8, simd_splat 8, all store_lane series), fixed each, and re-ran to confirm — a clear done/remaining picture at family granularity.

Computed the aggregate 32825/34212 = 0.9595 and quantified the concrete gap to 1.0 (the 1387 skipped assert_invalid/malformed assertions), knowing precisely what stood between current state and the bar.

The memory.json crash recurred across several iterations; the agent noticed it each cycle and pursued a new hypothesis (safer lookups, then capping memory allocation) rather than declaring victory, though it did not frame this as being 'stuck'.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, continuously refreshed picture of per-family pass counts by re-running the whole suite after each fix and enumerating exactly which families remained (steps 56,64,75,84,87-91), and it quantified the concrete remaining gap to 1.0 (the 1387 skipped assertions at step 93) — clearly above the level-5 'keeps a checklist and generally knows what remains.' It falls short of level 8/10 because progress was re-derived by re-running tests rather than tracked in a persistent ledger, it never explicitly reconciled implementation against the full listed opcode surface (trusting test files as proxy), and there is no evidence it caught a fix in one family breaking another. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 7.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized the absence of a validator means assert_invalid tests can't be caught natively; adapted strategy rather than barrelling ahead trying to catch them, though the eventual handling is closer to a workaround than a clean fix.
Stepped back on Br(N) branch semantics — diagnosed that propagation through block boundaries must decrement the depth, and reworked exec_block accordingly. A genuine semantic reconsideration.
Reconsidered conversion trap semantics after conversions family failed, distinguishing NaN/inf (invalid conversion) from out-of-range (integer overflow) in trunc_to.
Fixed falsified assumptions on load sign-extension and on v128.const being disallowed in const expressions — targeted semantic corrections localized from failing families.
Handled call_indirect/memory panics largely via local 'make lookups safer' patches rather than root-cause analysis, showing some patch-over-diagnose behavior.

On realizing score was 0.9595 due to skipped invalid tests, pivoted the assert_invalid handling to reach 1.0 — a structural recognition, but resolved by a scoring workaround rather than a clean refactor of a failure generator.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly stepped back and reconsidered specific assumptions when a family stubbornly failed — Br branch-depth semantics, conversion trap distinctions, load sign-extension, const-expr v128 — squarely matching the level-5 anchor, and its recognition of the missing-validator as a structural issue reaches toward level 8. However, several corrections were local safety patches rather than root-cause fixes, and the structural assert_invalid recognition was resolved via a scoring workaround rather than a clean shared-cause refactor that cleanly flips many assertions. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
